Commentary.Commentary: We are back with New Zealand's reply! The umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Tim Robinson and Will Young are the openers for New Zealand! Asitha Fernando is handed the new ball and will start the proceedings for Sri Lanka! Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The pitch offered no surprises, proving to be a paradise for the batters. With the downpour giving New Zealand a bit of a lifeline, they'll be eager to capitalize on the revised target ahead. As the conditions continue to favour the batters, the pitch is only expected to improve, and with the ball becoming harder to grip, Sri Lanka’s bowlers will need to be at their very best to defend this adjusted total. An electrifying finish is in store, so don’t go anywhere, the action is just moments away!

Just as New Zealand seemed to regain control, Charith Asalanka and Mendis struck a quick 53-run partnership, restoring Sri Lanka's momentum. Mendis eventually fell for a brilliant 143 off 128 balls, but Asalanka pressed on, boosting the total to 324/5 before rain interrupted. Jacob Duffy was a bright spot for New Zealand with three crucial wickets.

The Kiwi bowlers struggled to maintain pressure, appearing inconsistent and occasionally complacent, which allowed Kusal Mendis and Avishka Fernando to dominate effortlessly. Fielding lapses added to captain Mitchell Santner's frustration, with no bowling changes seeming to work. Both batters capitalized, each reaching centuries in a massive 206-run stand before Ish Sodhi finally dismissed Avishka. Michael Bracewell followed up by removing Sadeera Samarawickrama cheaply, offering some respite.

To recap the first innings, Sri Lanka delivered a commanding batting performance, closing their innings at 324/5 before rain cut things short with just four balls left. Opting to bat first after winning the toss, Sri Lanka got off to a promising start but faced an early hiccup when Pathum Nissanka was dismissed in the third over, despite a couple of elegant boundaries off Jacob Duffy. Avishka Fernando took time to find his footing, but Kusal Mendis stepped in with clarity and aggression, playing freely and relieving the mounting pressure. Once Avishka found his groove, the duo clicked beautifully, capitalizing on every loose delivery and crafting a partnership that stabilized the innings after the initial setback. Their solid partnership not only stabilized Sri Lanka after the early loss but also laid a strong foundation for a potential flourish in the final overs.

UPDATE - Finally, we have a restart time! The official word is in and we will resume at 3.40 pm GMT. The revised target for New Zealand will be 221 runs in 27 overs. Powerplay 1 will last for the first 6 overs, followed by Powerplay 2 until the 22nd over. Two bowlers are permitted to bowl a maximum of 6 overs each.

UPDATE - 3.23 pm GMT - The rain has stopped again in Dambulla. Hopefully, this time it will stay away so that we can see some more cricket. The ground staff have removed the covers and the umpires are out there for an inspection. We can safely say that even if we start now, we will have a shortened chase for New Zealand and we will know about the revised target pretty soon.

UPDATE - 3.04 pm GMT - Not the update we were hoping for! Just as the covers were being peeled back, the drizzle decided to make an untimely return, forcing the ground staff to spring into action once more. And so, the waiting game stretches on.

UPDATE - 2.49 pm GMT - Some positive news! It looks like the rain has stopped now and the covers are coming off too. We know that the ground staff here are excellent and they can prepare the ground pretty quickly barring further rain. However, we are still waiting for any official word on whether Sri Lanka will bat again or New Zealand will come out directly for the chase. Stick with us for more news!

UPDATE - 2.30 pm GMT - The waiting game drags on! With the time already lost, it's almost certain that once the rain clears, we'll be in for a shortened game. Could Sri Lanka’s decision to bat first come back to haunt them? Despite the uncertainty, they've posted a solid total, and now it’ll be up to New Zealand to bat out of their skins to stay on top of the equation considering rain as a factor.

UPDATE - 2.02 pm GMT - Still nothing new to update about. The weather forecast does not look good at the moment but we still have plenty of time to get some action and a result in this game. Meanwhile, the 3rd T20I between South Africa and India will begin in a short while with the four-match series level at 1-1. So, while we wait here, you can just switch tabs to enjoy all the build-up to that game.

UPDATE - 1.35 pm GMT - Unfortunately, the rain continues to fall persistently, and with the entire outfield now covered, it’s looking increasingly unlikely that we will see Sri Lanka bat again. It looks like the delay could extend for some time, and we might be heading towards a shortened game. If that’s the case, it could very well work in New Zealand's favour, as a reduced target might give them a better chance to chase while also making batting a bit easier. All said, we still await any official confirmation! Stay with us for any further updates on the situation.

Uh oh! The drizzle has intensified, and with just 4 balls left in the innings, the umpires have decided to call for the covers. The players are now off the field as the rain begins to make things tricky. We’ll have to wait and see how quickly the weather clears up and if the final few balls can be bowled. Stay tuned for further updates!

The stage is set for an exciting 3-match ODI series between Sri Lanka and New Zealand, following their drawn T20I series that ended 1-1. The ODIs will begin in Dambulla and conclude in Pallekele. For New Zealand, this series marks the final leg of their extensive subcontinent tour, which began with a rain-affected Test against Afghanistan in Noida, followed by a 0-2 series loss to Sri Lanka, before an impressive 3-0 whitewash of India. The hosts, Sri Lanka, view this as another opportunity to assert their dominance on home soil. Both teams have announced formidable squads ahead of the series. Under the leadership of the dynamic Charith Asalanka, Sri Lanka's batting lineup appears robust with in-form top order Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis. The middle order features skipper Asalanka himself, alongside rising star Kamindu Mendis, and experienced campaigners Kusal Perera and Sadeera Samarawickrama adding depth. Sri Lanka's bowling arsenal is spearheaded by their formidable spin duo of Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana, who are expected to be particularly effective in the local conditions. While spin remains their primary weapon with multiple options available, the pace department will depend on Dilshan Madushanka and Asitha Fernando with Mohamed Shiraz also another seam option. New Zealand faced a setback as Lockie Ferguson, who had just returned from a right hamstring injury, has been ruled out of the ODI series due to a calf injury sustained during the T20Is, right after taking a spectacular Hat Trick which helped New Zealand win by 5 wickets. The loss of the express pace bowler, known for habitually hitting speeds of 150 kph, deals a significant blow to the Kiwi bowling attack ahead of the series. New Zealand has announced a like-for-like replacement in the form of Adam Milne. Him, with 49 ODIs under his belt, will spearhead the pace attack alongside Jacob Duffy and newcomer Nathan Smith, while all-rounders Zakary Foulkes and Josh Clarkson provide additional bowling options. Captain Mitchell Santner, coming off a strong performance, will lead the spin department with Ish Sodhi.
